A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same D2A study. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original agent simulations, GPT-4o comparisons, human evaluations, ablations, and randomized-environment results in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds an outdoor averaged-dissatisfaction comparison in Section 6.3.3 and Figure 5.

M1.justification: The Value System, candidate proposal/evaluation/selection procedure, default planner width, and implementation prompts are retained. Appendix C.2 changes the planner analogy from MCTS to Tree of Thoughts, consistent with the procedure already described in v1 Section 5.3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate indoor activities, the outdoor party with background agents, and randomized indoor environments. The added outdoor plot concerns an existing scenario; changing Section 3 from 'indoor' to 'interactive' environments does not establish new task coverage.

E2.justification: ReAct, BabyAGI, and LLMob remain the comparison methods, alongside the retained human reference experiment. The new outdoor plot uses the same three baselines already represented in v1's outdoor analyses.

E3.justification: v2 adds an aggregate Random-8 dissatisfaction comparison in the existing outdoor setting, extending the quantitative evaluation beyond v1's outdoor case and diversity analyses. The retained indoor protocols, evaluation metrics, preprocessing, and backbone configurations are unchanged.

E4.justification: The indoor behavioral examples in v1 Appendices R–V are replaced by different trajectories in v2 Appendices P–T, revising qualitative evidence about repetitive behavior, including BabyAGI's food-focused example. The component, planner-width, multi-step-planning, Qwen, and randomized-environment analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Reported trial counts, 100 pairwise GPT-4o comparisons, three-run indoor dissatisfaction experiments, and uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged. The warning that the 42-step ablations lack standard deviations is retained; the new outdoor plot introduces no different statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 5 newly reports outdoor dissatisfaction trajectories for D2A and the three baselines, showing D2A reducing dissatisfaction in that setting. Indoor example sequences are also replaced. Matched existing heatmaps, Table 1, indoor curves, ablations, and randomized-environment results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), the expected-value mappings, and Appendix F's decay-probability formula are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central autonomy and human-like activity contributions remain. However, the abstract broadens its critique from task-oriented agents that often depend on explicit specifications to current AI agents generally, while the conclusion shifts its explicit adaptability claim from different LLMs to different motivational-framework configurations.

C2.justification: New Section 6.3.3 interprets the outdoor dissatisfaction results as evidence of generalization to social interaction settings. Section 6.3.1 changes BabyAGI's illustrative repetitive motivation from spiritual satisfaction to hunger. The stated limitations concerning simple desire dynamics and heuristic desire dimensions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Environment descriptions, trait/value mappings, D2A and baseline prompts, backbone information, Ollama integration information, and the project-page link are retained. Grouping prompts under Appendix J and relocating the Qwen discussion add no implementation or access details.

R1.justification: v2 adds Maslow (1943) and McClelland (1987) to substantiate the Theory of Needs motivation and removes the separate Qwen Team reference. Appendix C.2 corrects the MCTS analogy to Tree of Thoughts. The broader related-work positioning remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and polishes prose throughout the main text and case studies. It renames several sections, separates ablations into Section 6.4, groups D2A prompts under Appendix J, and relocates the Qwen discussion. The overall argument and document organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 5, rearranges the main ablation figure into three smaller horizontal panels, and moves the Qwen panel to Appendix O as Figure 14. Case-study annotations and captions are revised, and existing word clouds, tables, and randomized-environment figures are repositioned.

improvement.justification: Section 6.3.3 and Figure 5 add quantitative support for outdoor applicability beyond v1's case and diversity evidence. Clearer exposition, grouped prompts, and corrected planner terminology provide modest further benefits. The main evidence and limitations remain unchanged, while smaller main-text ablation panels slightly reduce readability.
